title: Fixed rational cochain retracts admit universally extended based homotopies
statement:
Let $M$ be a set. For each $m\in M$ let $(P_m^n,d_m^n)_{n\geq0}$ be a cochain complex of rational vector spaces, meaning $d_m^{n+1}d_m^n=0$, with a specified basis in each degree and cohomology defined by kernel modulo image, using the cochain reindexing of [def-weil-pbc-module-chain-complex-homology]. Let $K_m^n$ be based rational vector spaces with zero differential. Extend all terms by zero to negative degrees. Suppose rational linear maps $i_m^n:K_m^n\to P_m^n$ and $p_m^n:P_m^n\to K_m^n$ satisfy $d_mi_m=0$, $p_md_m=0$, $p_mi_m=1$, and $p_m$ induces an isomorphism
$$\ker d_m^n/\operatorname{im}d_m^{n-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}K_m^n$$
in every degree. Put $C_m^n=\ker p_m^n$ and $Z_m^n=\ker(d_m^n|_{C_m^n})$. Then $P_m=i_m(K_m)\oplus C_m$ as complexes, $C_m$ is acyclic, and there are rational subspaces $L_m^n$ with
$$C_m^n=Z_m^n\oplus L_m^n,\qquad d_m^n:L_m^n\xrightarrow{\sim}Z_m^{n+1}.$$
For any such choices, let $s_m^n:Z_m^n\to L_m^{n-1}$ be the inverse, with $s_m^0=0$ since $Z_m^0=0$. The prescription
$$h_m^n(i_mk+z+l)=s_m^n(z)\quad(k\in K_m^n,\ z\in Z_m^n,\ l\in L_m^n)$$
defines rational linear maps on $P=\bigoplus_mP_m$, preserving $m$, such that
$$h^0=0,\qquad dh+hd=1-ip,\qquad hi=0,\qquad ph=0,\qquad h^2=0.$$
Each basis vector has image a finite rational linear combination of basis vectors. For every commutative $\mathbf Q$-algebra $B$, including the zero algebra, replace each based space by the free $B$-module on the same basis and replace every rational matrix entry of $d,i,p,h$ by its image under $\mathbf Q\to B$. All these maps are well defined, and the same identities $d^2=0$, $di=0$, $pd=0$, $pi=1$, $dh+hd=1-ip$, $hi=ph=h^2=0$ hold over $B$. No finite-dimensionality, boundedness, or nonzero-algebra assumption is imposed.
For the particular constant cochain complex $P^n=\mathbf Q$ in every $n\geq0$, with $d^n=0$ for even $n$ and $d^n=1$ for odd $n$, and $K=\mathbf Q$ in degree zero, with $i,p$ identity in degree zero and zero otherwise, a choice of this homotopy is $h^n=1$ for even $n\geq2$ and $h^n=0$ otherwise; its matrix extension works over every $B$.

proof.text: Fix $m$ and suppress it. The map $q^n=1-i^np^n$ has image in $C^n$, since $pq=p-pip=0$, and fixes every element of $C^n$. Every $x\in P^n$ is $i(px)+q(x)$. If $i(k)\in C^n$, then $k=pi(k)=0$, so the decomposition is unique. Since $di=0$ and $pd=0$, the differential kills $i(K)$ and maps $C^n$ to $C^{n+1}$; also $dq=d=qd$. Thus this is a decomposition of complexes, with the specified $i,p$, not merely a degreewise decomposition.

proof.text: Let $z\in C^n$ satisfy $dz=0$. Its class in $H^n(P)=\ker d^n/\operatorname{im}d^{n-1}$ maps to $p(z)=0$. Injectivity of the hypothesized cohomology map gives $z=dy$ for some $y\in P^{n-1}$. Put $y_C=y-i(p(y))$; then $p(y_C)=0$ and $dy_C=dy=z$. Conversely $d^2=0$ makes every boundary in $C$ a cycle. Hence $Z^n=d(C^{n-1})$ and $C$ is acyclic. At $n=0$, the incoming term is zero, so the same argument gives $Z^0=0$. This uses the kernel-modulo-image meaning of cohomology in [def-weil-pbc-module-chain-complex-homology], with chain index $-n$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image for continuous coefficients; agent-written rational linear-algebra obligation extracted in lem-sfb-rational-polynomial-bar-contraction, fixed retraction and scalar-extension subargument.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-vector-subspace-complement] over the field $\mathbf Q$ to the subspace $Z_m^n\subseteq C_m^n$, for every $(m,n)$, choosing complements $L_m^n$ simultaneously over this set of indices. It gives unique decompositions $C_m^n=Z_m^n\oplus L_m^n$ without dimension restrictions. The restriction $d:L_m^n\to Z_m^{n+1}$ is injective because its kernel is $L_m^n\cap Z_m^n=0$. It is surjective: the preceding step gives $z=dc$, and writing $c=z_0+l$ gives $z=dl$. Its inverse is linear, since uniqueness of inverse images makes it preserve addition and rational scalar multiplication. Denote the inverse in degree $n$ by $s_m^n$; set $s_m^0=0$ on $Z_m^0=0$.

source.place: Submodule.exists_isCompl, lines 280–282; injectivity and surjectivity of the restricted differential computed explicitly from the preceding step.

proof.text: For any of these complement choices, unique decomposition defines the linear map $h^n(ik+z+l)=s^n(z)$ in each $m$. For $n\geq1$, $d^{n-1}h^n(ik+z+l)=z$, while $d^n(ik+z+l)=d^nl\in Z^{n+1}$ and $h^{n+1}d^n(ik+z+l)=s^{n+1}(d^nl)=l$. Their sum is $z+l=(1-ip)(ik+z+l)$. For $n=0$, $z=0$, $h^0=0$, and the second calculation alone gives the identity. Moreover $hi=0$ because $ik$ has zero $Z$-coordinate, and $ph=0$ because the image of $h$ lies in $L^{n-1}\subseteq C^{n-1}$. Finally $h^{n-1}s^n(z)=0$, since $s^n(z)$ lies in $L^{n-1}$ and has zero $Z^{n-1}$-coordinate; thus $h^2=0$, including the bottom degree.

proof.text: An element of $\bigoplus_m P_m^n$ has only finitely many nonzero $m$-components. Define $d,i,p,h$ on the corresponding direct sums componentwise. Each sends a component into the same $m$, so its output again has finite $m$-support. Addition, composition, and the identities just proved are checked in each component, which proves all asserted rational identities on the direct sums. This also covers $M=\varnothing$. In every specified basis the image of each basis vector under any of these linear maps is a finite rational linear combination, by the definition of a basis; the bases need not respect the chosen complements.

proof.text: Here is the scalar-extension calculation, for arbitrary sets of basis indices. Write a rational map $f:\mathbf Q^{(I)}\to\mathbf Q^{(J)}$ as $f(e_a)=\sum_{b\in S_a}f_{ba}e_b$ with $S_a$ finite. For $\alpha:\mathbf Q\to B$ define $f_B(\sum_{a\in T}b_ae_a)=\sum_{a\in T}\sum_{b\in S_a}b_a\alpha(f_{ba})e_b$, where $T$ is finite. Unique basis coefficients make this well defined and $B$-linear. If $g(e_b)=\sum_{c\in U_b}g_{cb}e_c$, then the composite on $e_a$ has support in the finite union $\bigcup_{b\in S_a}U_b$ and coefficient $\sum_{b\in S_a}\alpha(g_{cb})\alpha(f_{ba})=\alpha(\sum_{b\in S_a}g_{cb}f_{ba})$. Thus $(gf)_B=g_Bf_B$; the same finite calculation gives $(f+g)_B=f_B+g_B$, $0_B=0$ and $(1)_B=1$, and negatives follow from $\alpha(-r)=-\alpha(r)$. Apply these rules to each rational identity for $d,i,p,h$ proved above or assumed in the hypotheses. They give exactly all displayed identities over $B$. No injectivity of $\alpha$ is used; in particular the calculation holds when $B$ is the zero algebra. No infinite sum, finite-dimensionality, or boundedness enters.

proof.text: For the specified constant complex, $H^0=\mathbf Q$, and in positive even degrees the incoming differential is the identity while in odd degrees the outgoing differential is the identity, so all positive cohomology vanishes. The indicated $i,p$ therefore satisfy the hypotheses. Here $C^0=0$ and $C^n=\mathbf Q$ for $n\geq1$; $Z^n=C^n$ for even $n\geq2$ and $Z^n=0$ for odd $n$, so the only complements are $L^n=0$ for even $n$ and $L^n=C^n$ for odd $n\geq1$. Thus $s^n=(d^{n-1})^{-1}=1$ for even $n\geq2$, and the prescription of step 4 gives exactly $h^n=1$ for even $n\geq2$ and $h^n=0$ otherwise; this $h$ is therefore one (indeed the only) choice of the construction. With the stated $h$, in degree zero both $dh+hd$ and $1-ip$ are zero; in positive even degrees $d^{n-1}h^n=1$ and $h^{n+1}d^n=0$, while in odd degrees these are respectively $0$ and $1$. Every consecutive pair of homotopy components contains a zero map, so $h^2=0$; $hi=ph=0$ follows from $h^0=h^1=0$ and the degree support of $i,p$. All entries are $0$ or $1$, so the preceding finite-column calculation gives precisely this homotopy over every $B$.
